name: Force Field Analysis
use_case: A change-readiness technique that lists the forces pushing a proposed change forward and the forces holding it back, weights each one, and directs effort at weakening the restraints rather than adding more pressure. Best used when a change has stalled despite obvious benefits and repeated encouragement, because the reason it is stuck is almost always a restraining force nobody has named out loud.
strengths: reframes a stalled change from adding pressure to removing friction
weighting stops the loudest force being treated as the strongest
restraining forces are often invisible until the exercise names them
quick, and needs no data beyond the people in the room
weaknesses: forces are estimated subjectively and rarely validated
a snapshot: the balance shifts as the change proceeds
says nothing about sequencing or who acts
encourages tidy symmetric lists that hide one dominant restraint
use_cases: A hospital ward agreed a safer written handover routine, yet within weeks the nurses have slipped back to the old verbal handover and reminders from the matron have not changed that.
Staff voted for a new school homework policy last term, but most classrooms still do it the old way and the head teacher wants to know what is actually stopping teachers.
Two merged sales departments are meant to share one customer database, and every migration deadline slips although nobody openly objects to the plan.
I have tried several times to change a personal habit, such as exercising before work, and want to see clearly what keeps pulling me back to the old routine.
